hypotheses.title: Expired SSL certificate on external aa-fiu-gateway
hypotheses.mechanism: The SSL certificate for the external dependency aa-fiu-gateway expired precisely at 2026-10-08T13:30:00Z, causing all inbound SSL handshakes from aa-connector to fail immediately. This resulted in 100% failure rates in account linking and propagated errors upstream to mobile-bff.

supporting.note: Explicitly states SSL handshake failed because the certificate expired at notAfter=2026-10-08T13:30:00Z.
Shows FI fetch failed for consents with upstream errors starting at 13:30.
Error rate anomaly started precisely at 13:30.
Error rate anomaly started precisely at 13:30 due to synchronous calls to aa-connector.

assumptions: The external partner failed to renew or automate rotation of the aa-fiu-gateway certificate, explaining why internal metrics for aa-fiu-gateway showed normal request counts while connection attempts failed at the TLS handshake layer.

hypotheses.title: Regression introduced by aa-connector deployment chg-8692
hypotheses.mechanism: A bug introduced in aa-connector deployment chg-8692 caused incorrect TLS handling or certificate validation starting at a scheduled time.

supporting.note: Deploy on aa-connector occurred prior to the incident window.

contradicting.note: Log explicitly identifies an expired certificate (notAfter=2026-10-08T13:30:00Z) on the external gateway rather than a software regression.

assumptions: The deployment code was dormant until it triggered a certificate failure exactly at certificate expiration.

hypotheses.reasoning_summary: The symptom onset is clearly established at 2026-10-08T13:30:00+00:00 by metrics and log files. The primary hypothesis (H1) is overwhelmingly supported by log-00551, which details the exact SSL certificate expiration at the exact moment of onset. Although direct logs for aa-fiu-gateway were absent, the explicit TLS expiration timestamp in aa-connector's logs provides definitive proof of the external gateway's certificate expiration state. Alternative hypotheses like code deployment regressions (H2) remain heavily contradicted by the explicit certificate expiration details.
